title: Reports Made to Police for Circulation of AI-generated Fake Obscene Images
what_it_is: Reports Made to Police for Circulation of AI-generated Fake Obscene Images

sections.label: Police investigations of obscene material reports
sections.summary: Police investigate obscene material reports by interviewing the accused and witnesses and examining digital forensic evidence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Where there is a report relating to any obscene material, the Police will conduct investigations, including through interviewing the accused and other witnesses, and examining any digital forensic evidence that may be available.

sections.label: Online Criminal Harms Act directions
sections.summary: Police may direct online service providers to disable Singapore users' access to circulating AI-generated obscene images.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: If the AI-generated obscene images are circulating online, the Police may issue directions under the Online Criminal Harms Act to online service providers to disable Singapore users’ access to them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The first is that in some cases that I have come across, I was told by the victims that they reported to Police that their images had been artificially created and put up on porn websites, and the Police had advised them to take action under the Protection from Harassment Act, as it is a non-arrestable offence.

sections.label: Penal Code intimate image offences
sections.summary: Police will act under Penal Code offences for circulating intimate images if the facts warrant it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The third question is, I believe that under the Penal Code, there are actually some arrestable offences that would actually cover some of the conduct – for example, being in possession of intimate images and so on, under section 377BD and 377BE.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask when the Police would classify the case under these arrestable offences and investigate with the view to prosecution.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: I would say that if the facts of the case are such that it warrants taking action under the Penal Code for offences relating to the circulation of intimate images, the Police will do so.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: So, it is not that there is a default position to go a certain route – everything depends on the facts of the case as disclosed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: In terms of what happens to the images that are, say, circulating online, as I have also shared in the main reply, where there are obscene images circulating online, and which, in the course of investigation, or due to the report, it is known, the Police may issue directions to the online service providers to block access of Singapore users to them.
